title: Add AUR publishing to release workflow
eaRS Parakeet Streaming Engine - Epic
description:
# eaRS Parakeet Streaming Engine - Epic

## Goal
Implement a robust Parakeet ASR engine for eaRS that provides real-time streaming transcription with deduplication and overlap handling, replacing the initial chunked approach that produced duplicate words.

## Background
eaRS is a real-time speech-to-text server supporting multiple ASR engines (Kyutai, Parakeet, Moonshine). The Parakeet engine was added to provide a lightweight, offline-capable alternative to the cloud-based Kyutai engine. Parakeet is a non-streaming RNN-T model that works by processing fixed-size audio chunks independently.

**Key architectural challenge:** Since Parakeet processes chunks independently (no state carryover), each chunk produces slightly different token alignments for overlapping audio regions, which caused duplicate words in the streaming output.

## Architecture

### Core Files
- `src/server/parakeet.rs` - Parakeet engine implementation (661 lines)
- `src/server/engine.rs` - Engine trait definitions
- `src/server/` - Server infrastructure

### Key Components

**ParakeetEngine** (lines 86-122):
- Loads model from HuggingFace via `prkt::ParakeetModel::load_from_hf()`
- Configures chunk size (default 3s) and overlap (default 1s) at 24kHz sample rate
- Supports multiple backends: CPU, CoreML (Apple), CUDA, ROCm, DirectML
- Thread-safe via `Arc<Mutex<prkt::ParakeetModel>>` and semaphore-based session limiting

**ParakeetSessionHandle** (lines 167-195):
- Implements `EngineSession` trait
- Manages audio/control channels for each session
- Handles `send_audio()`, `set_language()`, `request_stop()`, `supports_language()`

**run_parakeet_session()** (lines 247-553):
- Main processing loop
- Receives audio via unbounded channel, buffers at 24kHz
- VAD processing with webrtc_vad (aggressive mode, 16kHz)
- Chunked transcription with overlap handling
- Word deduplication via timestamp-based overlap detection

### Streaming Strategy
1. Audio arrives in chunks (default 80ms) at 24kHz
2. Buffer accumulates until `chunk_samples_24k` (3s default)
3. Transcribe first `chunk_samples_24k` samples
4. Shift overlap region (1s default) for next chunk
5. Deduplicate overlap words against `committed_words` using timestamp partitioning
6. Emit only new words to WebSocket client

### Deduplication Algorithm
- **Timestamp-based**: Split transcribed words into overlap (before `chunk_start_time + overlap_duration`) and new regions
- **Overlap handling**: Match overlap words against tail of `committed_words` using `word_match_ratio()` (LCS-based fuzzy matching)
- **Correction logic**: If overlap match ratio < 0.4, trust new transcription and replace old words
- **New words**: Always emitted without filtering

### Test Results (After Fixes)
- **Short clips (3-5s)**: Perfect accuracy, 0 duplicates, RTF ~1.05x
  - english_00.wav (3.5s): 8/8 words, 0 duplicates
  - english_02.wav (5.0s): 10/10 words, 0 duplicates
  - english_08.wav (4.8s): 9/9 words, 0 duplicates
- **Long clips (10s+)**: Truncation mid-stream, Parakeet stuck in empty-chunk loop

### Configuration
```rust
pub struct ParakeetEngineConfig {
    pub model_repo: String,           // HuggingFace repo (default: "Kyutai/parakeet-1b")
    pub model_dir: Option<PathBuf>,   // Local model cache
    pub device: ParakeetDevice,       // Cpu, CoreML, Cuda, ROCm, DirectML
    pub chunk_seconds: f32,           // Default 3.0s
    pub overlap_seconds: f32,         // Default 1.0s
    pub noise_gate_rms: f32,          // Silence threshold
}
```

## Completed Work
- ✅ Buffer trim bug fix (only trim when words produced, preventing audio loss)
- ✅ Timestamp-based overlap deduplication (replaces naive prefix matching)
- ✅ Fuzzy word matching for overlap correction (LCS-based ratio)
- ✅ VAD integration with pause detection
- ✅ Noise gate support
- ✅ Test infrastructure (bench_streaming.py, test audio samples)

## Known Issues
- Long clip truncation: Parakeet returns empty chunks repeatedly for audio >10s
- Benchmark script uses IPv4 address but server listens on IPv6 only
- Server hangs/crashes during initial model load (race condition or memory issue)

## Dependencies
- `prkt` crate for Parakeet model inference
- `webrtc_vad` for voice activity detection
- `kaudio` for resampling (24kHz → 16kHz)
- `rubato` for audio resampling (indirect dependency)

## Next Steps
- Fix long clip truncation (see trx issue for buffer trim safety limit)
- Add safety limit to prevent infinite empty-chunk loops
- Fix benchmark script IPv6 address
- Investigate server startup crash

title: Fix long clip truncation in Parakeet streaming
Deterministic voice command mode for eaRS dictation
description: Add an explicit command-capture mode alongside normal eaRS dictation. A VAD-bounded utterance is normalized through the existing dictionary, matched deterministically against data-authored command definitions, checked against static execution policy (and optional speaker-identification evidence), then either dispatched to a constrained action adapter or rejected. Runtime contains no LLM judgment; a companion skill may inspect the host and author/review configuration. Commands must never execute from partial streaming text or interpolate free-form voice text into a shell.

title: Define command schema, matcher, and utterance pipeline
description: Create XDG TOML command definitions plus JSON Schema, hot reload, canonical text matching, and an utterance pipeline: VAD-bounded raw transcript -> dictionary normalization -> exact command match. Preserve raw/normalized text for audit. In command capture, buffer word events until Speech(false); do not type or execute partial text. Unknown/ambiguous phrases execute nothing and may optionally fall back to typing only under explicit policy. Tests must prove dictionary-before-command ordering, split stream events, ambiguity rejection, and no partial execution.

title: Implement three routing modes and global voice mode controls
description: Implement an explicit utterance-routing state machine integrated with existing toggle/push-to-talk/hybrid capture controls. Three canonical modes: (1) dictation: ordinary words keep the current low-latency streaming path; globally reserved, exact `eaRS ...` control utterances are consumed; (2) command-aware: each utterance is buffered to Speech(false), configured commands execute, unmatched utterances are typed atomically; (3) command-only: each utterance is buffered, configured commands execute, unmatched utterances are discarded. Reserved controls must be recognized in every mode so the user cannot become trapped: `eaRS dictation mode`, `eaRS command-aware mode`, `eaRS command-only mode`, `eaRS start typing`, `eaRS stop typing`, `eaRS cancel`, and `eaRS what mode`. Hold only a possible leading `eaRS` prefix in streaming dictation so normal live typing remains immediate. In command-only mode, start typing opens a temporary streaming dictation substate and stop typing returns to command-only. Mode changes are exact whole-utterance matches, optionally speaker-gated, and always have a hotkey escape. Provide visible/audible state feedback, never leak consumed control/command text into the focused application, and test every transition, unknown utterances, cancellation, streaming prefix handling, and configured restart defaults.

title: Implement constrained command action adapters and policy
description: Implement deterministic adapters for keyboard shortcuts, literal text, executable argv/script paths, and narrowly-scoped platform actions. Never pass spoken text to sh -c or interpolate arbitrary captures by default. Add timeout, cwd/env allowlists, single-flight execution, audit records, and static risk tiers. Safe actions may run immediately; consequential/destructive actions require explicit confirmation. Test injection resistance, timeout, confirmation, and fail-closed behavior.

title: Integrate optional enrolled-speaker evidence for command gating
description:
Consume the shared voqx Voice Identity registry (voqx-core) and its optional WeSpeaker recognition profiles via `voqx_core::{VoiceRegistry, RegistryStore}` — do NOT couple eaRS to trnscrb internals or stand up a separate speaker store. See voqx `docs/adr/0001-voice-identity-model.md`.

For each command utterance, derive speaker evidence from the same VAD-bounded audio and join it with the normalized transcript before dispatch. eaRS receives evidence only, of the shape `{ voice_id, display_name, score, status }` (status = Confident/Tentative/Unknown/InsufficientAudio/IncompatibleModel); it never parses embeddings or registry files directly.

Treat recognition as identification / accidental-trigger suppression, NOT strong authentication: replay and short-utterance limitations remain. Unknown/low-confidence speaker must fail closed for configured commands; destructive actions still require confirmation regardless of speaker. Benchmark latency and calibrate thresholds (voqx `Thresholds`, defaults confident>=0.60 / tentative>=0.45) with multiple enrolled samples.

title: Create skill-driven command setup and audit workflow
description: Design a public skill that inventories OS, installed apps, existing CLI tools, and user-selected workflows; proposes command phrases/actions/risk tiers; asks before writing; validates against the schema; and runs dry-run tests. The skill owns setup judgment while eaRS runtime remains deterministic. Do not automatically expose every discovered executable or shortcut.

title: Build standalone personalized wake-word detector and eaRS adapter
description:
Build a standalone, library-first Rust wake tool (its own repo, e.g. ../wake) with eaRS/Foxline as consumers. Do NOT reintroduce sherpa-onnx. MVP backend: rustpotter 3.x (Apache-2.0, pure Rust MFCC+DTW) with 3-8 personalized references for immediate use; promotion path trains Rustpotter Tiny (~320KB)/Small (~768KB) models; pure-Rust openWakeWord via oww-rs/tract only as a fallback if false-accept/false-reject targets are missed. Multi-label models may back a small, stable Tier-0/Tier-1 acoustic control vocabulary; the editable TOML command registry stays transcription-based (no retrain on config edit).

Ownership / registry contract: the wake tool owns wake model artifacts, training, evaluation, calibration, and streaming detection ONLY. Enrollment and identity are owned by voqx: guided recording, reusable source recordings, and the stable `voice_id` live in the voqx Voice Identity registry (voqx-core). Each wake profile references a `voice_id` (see voqx WakeProfile) rather than creating its own speaker/identity store. `voqx wake enroll` records phrase takes on a voice_id and may shell out to the wake trainer. spqx may supply synthetic positives.

Audio: single capture owner. eaRS owns the microphone and tees 16 kHz PCM frames to the detector (embedded lib call or Unix-socket PCM); the wake tool must not open its own capture except for standalone enrollment/testing. Runtime output is detection evidence only ({label/phrase, voice_id?, score, timestamp}); dictionary, command matching, speaker policy, confirmations, and action execution stay downstream in eaRS/Foxline. eaRS's mode state machine (trx-2stp.2) arbitrates what a detection means. Measure false accepts/hour, false rejects, latency, CPU/RAM, replay, microphones, noise, and non-owner voices.

title: Fix dictation stop hook not firing on ears dictation is not running.
Regex-capable replacement rules for text normalization (data-authored)
description:
Rescoped from "server-side EN+DE ITN rule engine" after a bitter-lesson audit: a compiled-in per-language ITN rule engine hand-codes linguistic knowledge that ASR checkpoints learn better each year (English Nemotron already emits written-form numbers natively), and supporting a new language would require recompiling eaRS.

New scope:
1. Extend the existing replacement/dictionary pipeline to support regex rules (pattern -> replacement with capture groups), authored as data in dictionary TOML files. eaRS stays a deterministic transform of (audio, rules) -> text; zero linguistic judgment compiled into the core.
2. Ship an optional example dictionary with common EN/DE spoken-number/currency normalizations so operators can opt in.
3. Document the model-selection fix: spoken-form output is primarily a checkpoint weakness (multilingual Nemotron 3.5); prefer written-form-strong models (English Nemotron, transcribe.cpp multitalker-parakeet) where possible.

Out of scope: any built-in per-language ITN engine. Long-tail multilingual ITN belongs in the judgment layer (Foxline LLM post-pass), not eaRS.

This no longer blocks transcribe.cpp integration (trx-ffpf) - that integration IS the scaling fix for written-form output.

title: Add global dictionary-based transcript replacement
description: Implement a global dictionary-based string replacement pass for eaRS dictation/transcription. Start with global dictionary config/file support where multiple observed phrases map to one canonical replacement, expose CLI commands to list/add/test dictionary entries, apply replacement client-side in ears-dictation before typing final transcripts, and store typed transcript history in XDG state as JSONL for future suggestion tooling. Proof: unit tests for multi-phrase replacement, CLI test/list behavior, cargo check, and a documented example dictionary.
close_reason: Fixed dictionary conflict behavior so phrases are unique across replacements, corrected global oqto/octo entries, added dictation hot reload of dictionary files, and validated with replacement tests plus cargo check.

title: Ship Linux ARM64 prebuilt (CPU) via Cross.toml
description:
# Context

eaRS migrated from cargo-dist to the byteowlz standard matrix release.yml
(templates-repo/rust-workspace). Linux x86_64 CPU binaries now ship natively on
ubuntu-latest (apt installs libasound2-dev, libdbus-1-dev, libssl-dev), so the
old cargo-dist/zigbuild sysroot problem is gone.

# Remaining work

Linux ARM64 (aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu) is disabled by default in the standard
workflow. Enabling it needs a Cross.toml with OpenSSL config per the workflow's
commented matrix entry (`cross: true`).

# Non-goals

- GPU on Linux stays source-only (build with --features cuda); prebuilt CUDA
  binaries are too coupled to driver/toolkit versions to ship.

# Acceptance

- [ ] aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu CPU tarball builds green in the release workflow
- [ ] Cross.toml committed with the OpenSSL configuration

title: Ensure dictation start validates server availability (local/remote)
Test, bump version, and commit strict dictation startup checks
Local per-repo dictation dictionaries with ears dict alias
description:
Add repo-scoped dictation dictionaries so domain terms (model names, engine names, crate names) are corrected only in the relevant repo, keeping the global dictionary lean.

## Motivation
The global dictionary (~/.config/ears/dictionaries/global.toml) currently holds every term across all byteowlz tools. Repo-specific vocabulary (e.g. eaRS: Nemotron, transcribe-cpp, Voxtral, GGUF, committed/tentative, barge-in) does not belong in the global dictionary a user loads everywhere. ReplacementConfig.dictionary_paths is already a Vec<String>, so the merge plumbing exists; what is missing is per-repo file management, config wiring, and a shorter CLI surface.

## Scope
1. Rename the 'dictionary' subcommand to 'dict' (keep 'dictionary' as a backward-compatible alias).
2. New 'ears dict local' subcommand group to create and manage a dictionary scoped to the current repo.
3. Two storage locations, user choice:
   - Personal (default): ~/.config/ears/dictionaries/<repo-name>.toml (private, never committed)
   - Repo-included (--commit): <repo-root>/dictation/dictionary.toml (version-controlled, shared with the team)
4. 'ears dict local init' auto-detects the repo root, creates the dict file, and injects its path into replacement.dictionary_paths in config.toml (manual mapping, no auto tmux/cwd detection in this epic).

## Non-goals
- Automatic repo detection from tmux/herder pane cwd (possible future work; manual mapping is acceptable).
- Speaker-scoped dictionaries.

## Related
- Skill: dictation-auditor (interactive read-aloud mispronunciation capture) lives in skillissues, consumes this CLI.
- Coexists with ctx (context capture) but does not depend on it.

title: Rename dictionary subcommand to dict with backward-compat alias
description:
Rename the clap 'Dictionary' subcommand to 'dict' and keep 'dictionary' working as an alias so existing scripts and docs do not break.

## Changes
- src/main.rs: rename Commands::Dictionary variant handling to 'dict'; add #[command(visible_alias = "dictionary")] (or aliases) so both invocations resolve to the same handler.
- Update README.md and any --help examples to use 'ears dict ...'.
- Keep DictionaryCommand subcommands (list/add/remove/test) unchanged.

## Acceptance
- 'ears dict list', 'ears dict add', 'ears dict remove', 'ears dict test' all work.
- 'ears dictionary list' still works (alias).
- cargo check passes.
- README uses 'ears dict' as the primary form.

title: Implement ears dict local subcommand group
description:
Add 'ears dict local' to create and manage a dictionary scoped to the current repository.

## Subcommands
- 'ears dict local init [--commit]' - detect repo root (git rev-parse --show-toplevel), create the local dict file, and add its path to replacement.dictionary_paths in config.toml if not already present.
  - Default location (personal): ~/.config/ears/dictionaries/<repo-name>.toml
  - With --commit: <repo-root>/dictation/dictionary.toml (version-controlled). Do NOT auto 'git add'; print a hint instead.
- 'ears dict local list' - show which repos have local dicts and their on-disk paths / config wiring status.
- 'ears dict local add --replacement CANON --phrase OBS' - add to the current repo's local dict (resolve which file via repo detection).
- 'ears dict local remove ...' - inverse of add.
- 'ears dict local test TEXT' - run replacement using global + local merged, so users can verify.

## Config wiring
- On init, read config.toml, append the new path to replacement.dictionary_paths (idempotent), write back preserving formatting where practical.
- Global dictionary stays first in the list; local dict appended after so LeftmostLongest still prefers the most specific phrase.

## Detection
- Repo root via 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel'; error clearly if not in a git repo (suggest --path override).
- <repo-name> derived from the repo root directory name.

## Acceptance
- 'ears dict local init' inside eaRS creates ~/.config/ears/dictionaries/eaRS.toml and wires it into config.toml.
- 'ears dict local init --commit' creates eaRS/dictation/dictionary.toml instead.
- 'ears dict local add' writes to the correct repo dict; 'ears dict test' reflects the merged result.
- cargo check passes; unit tests cover repo-root detection and idempotent config injection.

title: dictation-auditor skill: interactive read-aloud mispronunciation capture
description:
Author a skill (in byteowlz/skillissues/skills/dictation-auditor) that builds a repo-scoped dictation dictionary by watching how eaRS actually mishears domain terms.

## Workflow the skill drives
1. Scan the target repo for domain terms: struct/enum/trait names, crate names, CLI names, acronyms, model/engine names, product names. Rank by frequency and importance.
2. Read the existing global dictionary and (if present) the repo's local dict; drop any term already covered.
3. Present the remaining terms in SMALL batches (5-7 at a time) as short read-aloud phrases/sentences, never a wall of text, so the user can digest and speak them.
4. For each batch, the user dictates via eaRS while the skill captures what eaRS typed (from transcript history JSONL, and/or 'ears dict test'). It records the mispronunciations / raw phrases.
5. Match observed raw phrases to canonical terms; propose conservative entries.
6. Tag each suggested entry GLOBAL (cross-project term) or LOCAL (repo-specific term) so the user decides where it goes.
7. Emit a ready-to-review TOML plus the exact 'ears dict add' / 'ears dict local add' commands. Do not mutate dictionaries without explicit approval.

## Notes
- Reuse heuristics and transcript-mining approach from the existing ears-dictionary-suggestions skill; this skill adds the interactive read-aloud capture loop and the GLOBAL/LOCAL tagging.
- Depends on the 'ears dict local' CLI (trx-dptk.2) for the LOCAL side; can degrade to global-only suggestions until that lands.

## Acceptance
- SKILL.md exists in skillissues with the batched read-aloud workflow.
- Skill classifies each suggestion GLOBAL vs LOCAL with a stated reason.
- Skill never dumps a wall of text; batches are 5-7 terms.
- Skill asks before writing to any dictionary.

title: Seed eaRS local dictation dictionary with domain terms
description:
Once 'ears dict local' exists, populate the eaRS repo-local dictionary with eaRS-specific vocabulary that should NOT live in the global dictionary.

## Candidate LOCAL terms (repo-specific)
Model/engine names: Nemotron, Voxtral, multitalker-parakeet, transcribe-cpp, handy-computer, ParakeetRs, TranscribeCpp, GGUF, GGML, Q8_0/Q5_K_M/Q4_K_M quant tokens.
Streaming concepts: committed, tentative, revisable transcript, speech boundary, VAD hangover, barge-in, noise gate, resample, compute lease.
Audio: PCM, OGG Opus, 24 kHz, 16 kHz, sample rate, sentencepiece.

## Candidate GLOBAL terms (belong in global.toml, not here)
Moshi, Sherpa ONNX (already partly present), streaming ASR, real-time - verify these are in global before adding locally.

## Process
- Prefer running the dictation-auditor skill (trx-dptk.3) to capture REAL mispronunciations rather than guessing phrases.
- Only hand-seed obvious high-frequency terms if the skill workflow is not yet available.

## Acceptance
- eaRS local dict contains the eaRS-specific terms above with observed (not invented) phrase variants where possible.
- No eaRS-specific term is added to the global dictionary.

title: Integrate transcribe.cpp as engine (streaming + offline transcription)
description:
Unblocked from trx-5xj3: ITN was rescoped to data-authored regex replacement rules and no longer gates engine work. Integrating transcribe.cpp (multitalker-parakeet Q8 for EN, nemotron-3.5 Q8 multilingual) is itself the primary fix for spoken-form output, since its best EN models emit written form natively.

Benchmarks (M4 Max, Q8, Metal, 560ms streaming): multitalker-parakeet 3.37%/5.82% WER ~34x RT; nemotron-3.5 5.62%/15.87% ~30x; voxtral-mini-realtime 1.12%/5.29% ~4.7x. Baseline eaRS parakeet-rs: 4.49%/6.88% ~11x.
close_reason: Integrated as feature-gated engine; verified 3.37% WER end-to-end with multitalker-parakeet Q8 on Metal

title: test
Dictation UX + durability borrows from jot-gemini (Gemini Transcribe demo)
description:
## Why

Eval'd google-gemini/jot-gemini-transcribe-macOS (wiki `external-repo-evals/jot-gemini.md`, verdict watch). It is a macOS smart-dictation demo on hosted Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, but several patterns are borrowable into ears' local STT/dictation surface. File as a spike/reference direction, not an engine swap (ears = local STT via eaRS; Jot = hosted Gemini STT, macOS-only).

## Borrowable patterns to evaluate

1. **Dictation UX** — hold-to-talk (`fn` hold / `fn`+Space hands-free / Esc cancel), no-window, text lands at cursor in the app in use. Compare with ears' current voice-input surface; spike the cursor-insert + gesture model.
2. **Audio durability** — audio written to disk from the first millisecond; crash/kill-9/battery costs nothing (recording recovered on next launch); offline dictations queue and land on reconnect; every failure retryable from History. Maps to ears' audio handling — worth a spike.
3. **LLM formatting pipeline** — JotCore FormattingPipeline (`ReplacementEngine` + `PromptV1` + `ValidationGate`): punctuate, remove filler, "follow a change of mind" ("1pm — actually no, 2pm" → "2pm"). ears already has regex replacement rules (trx-5xj3); evaluate whether a small LLM-cleanup stage adds value over regex.
4. **Privacy-by-architecture** — voice → API direct with the user's own key, no middleman server/analytics/keystroke-logging. Confirm ears' local-STT posture keeps this; relevant to govnr sensitive-data rule.

## Outcome

Decide per pattern: adopt / adapt / reject. Prefer small evidence-producing spikes (per govnr idea-management). Revisit the wiki eval on trigger.

## Reference
- wiki: `external-repo-evals/jot-gemini.md` (remote_url, analysis_date 2026-08-08, analyzed_for ears)

title: Add sherpa-onnx engine for multilingual streaming STT on CPU
description:
# Add sherpa-onnx engine for multilingual streaming STT on CPU

## Goal
Provide a high-quality, FOSS streaming ASR engine that runs well on CPU as an alternative to the Kyutai engine. Target use case: dictation and live transcription in multiple languages (en/de/fr/es minimum) with low latency and accuracy comparable to or better than Whisper-large-v3.

The "north star" is parity with Microsoft Teams' live captions, but fully local and FOSS.

## Why sherpa-onnx
After investigating Parakeet's chunked-streaming behavior we found that Parakeet-TDT 0.6B is fundamentally non-streaming (RNN-T encoder is not cache-aware). Chunked inference produced 8-10× worse WER than one-shot on the same audio (Tommy_1: 5.3% one-shot → 43.9% chunked at 3s; Tommy_3: 1.3% → 76%).

sherpa-onnx (k2-fsa) provides natively streaming architectures and ships ready-to-use ONNX models:

- **Zipformer2 streaming** — cache-state streaming, multilingual variants available, low latency
- **NeMo Canary-180m-flash** — en/de/fr/es, 1.87% LibriSpeech clean / 4-5% MLS de/es/fr, 1200+ RTFx on GPU and runs at int8 on CPU
- **NeMo Parakeet-TDT-CTC-110M streaming** — already exported by sherpa-onnx
- **FastConformer cache-aware streaming**
- **Paraformer** (Chinese) for completeness

License: Apache 2.0. Rust bindings: `sherpa-rs` crate (mature, actively maintained).

## Acceptance criteria

1. New `sherpa` engine selectable via `--engine sherpa` in eaRS server, sitting alongside `kyutai` and `parakeet`.
2. Cargo feature `sherpa` (gated, default-off, like `parakeet`).
3. CPU path works without GPU (primary requirement). GPU optional via existing `nvidia`/`apple`/`directml` feature flags if sherpa-rs supports them.
4. Streaming WebSocket protocol matches existing Kyutai/Parakeet: `Word { text, start_time }` and `Step { step_idx }` messages.
5. Configurable model selection in `~/.config/eaRS/config.toml`:
   - Model family (zipformer2-streaming, canary-180m-flash, parakeet-tdt-ctc-110m)
   - Model URL or local path
   - Language (passed to Canary multilingual variant)
6. WER on Tommy_1.wav and Tommy_3.wav ≤ 8% (i.e., closer to one-shot Parakeet quality than chunked Parakeet).
7. End-to-end latency ≤ 500 ms first-word on CPU for the smallest model.
8. Dictation binary (`ears-dictation`) works with sherpa engine on Linux (uinput) — no regressions.

## Non-goals
- Replacing Kyutai. This is an additional engine, not a swap.
- GPU optimization on launch — CPU-first.
- Translation. Canary supports it, but this ticket is ASR only.

## Open questions
- Which Zipformer2 streaming model is the multilingual default? Investigate `sherpa-onnx-streaming-zipformer-multi-zh-hans-2023-12-12` vs newer multilingual exports.
- How does sherpa-rs handle dynamic dlopen of onnxruntime? May avoid the protobuf-lite collision we hit with `ort` directly. If not, reuse the `ORT_DYLIB_PATH`/`load-dynamic` pattern from trx-1pms.1.
- Word-level timestamps: sherpa-onnx exposes them per-token; need to confirm they're carried through sherpa-rs.

## Implementation sketch
1. Add optional `sherpa-rs` dependency behind `sherpa` feature.
2. New module `src/server/sherpa.rs` mirroring `parakeet.rs` structure: streaming session loop, audio resampling to model's expected sample rate (16 kHz for Zipformer2, 16 kHz for Canary), word emission.
3. Reuse the empty-chunk safety counter pattern from trx-1pms.1 as a defensive guard.
4. Model download: prefer hf-hub for HuggingFace-hosted exports; fall back to direct URL for k2-fsa GitHub releases.
5. CLI: `ears-server --engine sherpa --sherpa-model zipformer2-streaming-multilingual`.
6. Tests: extend `bench_streaming.py` to cover the new engine; add Tommy_1/Tommy_3 WER regression check.

## References
- sherpa-onnx: https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx
- sherpa-rs: https://github.com/thewh1teagle/sherpa-rs
- nvidia/canary-180m-flash: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/canary-180m-flash
- HF Open ASR Leaderboard: https://huggingface.co/spaces/hf-audio/open_asr_leaderboard

## Related
- Supersedes trx-xv0t (Moonshine — English-only, didn't fit multilingual goal)
- Builds on lessons from trx-1pms.1 (Parakeet streaming truncation fix)

- EARS_DEBUG_DIR=/path overrides the output directory.

- ws-sessions.log: WebSocket ingress counters.

ws-sessions.log records once per active session per second, including idle periods:
- audio_msgs/audio_samples received from the client

- send_audio_ok/send_audio_err from forwarding into the engine session
- text_msgs/close_msgs

title: eaRS Parakeet Streaming Engine - Epic
description:
# eaRS Parakeet Streaming Engine - Epic

## Goal
Implement a robust Parakeet ASR engine for eaRS that provides real-time streaming transcription with deduplication and overlap handling, replacing the initial chunked approach that produced duplicate words.

## Background
eaRS is a real-time speech-to-text server supporting multiple ASR engines (Kyutai, Parakeet, Moonshine). The Parakeet engine was added to provide a lightweight, offline-capable alternative to the cloud-based Kyutai engine. Parakeet is a non-streaming RNN-T model that works by processing fixed-size audio chunks independently.

**Key architectural challenge:** Since Parakeet processes chunks independently (no state carryover), each chunk produces slightly different token alignments for overlapping audio regions, which caused duplicate words in the streaming output.

## Architecture

### Core Files
- `src/server/parakeet.rs` - Parakeet engine implementation (661 lines)
- `src/server/engine.rs` - Engine trait definitions
- `src/server/` - Server infrastructure

### Key Components

**ParakeetEngine** (lines 86-122):
- Loads model from HuggingFace via `prkt::ParakeetModel::load_from_hf()`
- Configures chunk size (default 3s) and overlap (default 1s) at 24kHz sample rate
- Supports multiple backends: CPU, CoreML (Apple), CUDA, ROCm, DirectML
- Thread-safe via `Arc<Mutex<prkt::ParakeetModel>>` and semaphore-based session limiting

**ParakeetSessionHandle** (lines 167-195):
- Implements `EngineSession` trait
- Manages audio/control channels for each session
- Handles `send_audio()`, `set_language()`, `request_stop()`, `supports_language()`

**run_parakeet_session()** (lines 247-553):
- Main processing loop
- Receives audio via unbounded channel, buffers at 24kHz
- VAD processing with webrtc_vad (aggressive mode, 16kHz)
- Chunked transcription with overlap handling
- Word deduplication via timestamp-based overlap detection

### Streaming Strategy
1. Audio arrives in chunks (default 80ms) at 24kHz
2. Buffer accumulates until `chunk_samples_24k` (3s default)
3. Transcribe first `chunk_samples_24k` samples
4. Shift overlap region (1s default) for next chunk
5. Deduplicate overlap words against `committed_words` using timestamp partitioning
6. Emit only new words to WebSocket client

### Deduplication Algorithm
- **Timestamp-based**: Split transcribed words into overlap (before `chunk_start_time + overlap_duration`) and new regions
- **Overlap handling**: Match overlap words against tail of `committed_words` using `word_match_ratio()` (LCS-based fuzzy matching)
- **Correction logic**: If overlap match ratio < 0.4, trust new transcription and replace old words
- **New words**: Always emitted without filtering

### Test Results (After Fixes)
- **Short clips (3-5s)**: Perfect accuracy, 0 duplicates, RTF ~1.05x
  - english_00.wav (3.5s): 8/8 words, 0 duplicates
  - english_02.wav (5.0s): 10/10 words, 0 duplicates
  - english_08.wav (4.8s): 9/9 words, 0 duplicates
- **Long clips (10s+)**: Truncation mid-stream, Parakeet stuck in empty-chunk loop

### Configuration
```rust
pub struct ParakeetEngineConfig {
    pub model_repo: String,           // HuggingFace repo (default: "Kyutai/parakeet-1b")
    pub model_dir: Option<PathBuf>,   // Local model cache
    pub device: ParakeetDevice,       // Cpu, CoreML, Cuda, ROCm, DirectML
    pub chunk_seconds: f32,           // Default 3.0s
    pub overlap_seconds: f32,         // Default 1.0s
    pub noise_gate_rms: f32,          // Silence threshold
}
```

## Completed Work
- ✅ Buffer trim bug fix (only trim when words produced, preventing audio loss)
- ✅ Timestamp-based overlap deduplication (replaces naive prefix matching)
- ✅ Fuzzy word matching for overlap correction (LCS-based ratio)
- ✅ VAD integration with pause detection
- ✅ Noise gate support
- ✅ Test infrastructure (bench_streaming.py, test audio samples)

## Known Issues
- Long clip truncation: Parakeet returns empty chunks repeatedly for audio >10s
- Benchmark script uses IPv4 address but server listens on IPv6 only
- Server hangs/crashes during initial model load (race condition or memory issue)

## Dependencies
- `prkt` crate for Parakeet model inference
- `webrtc_vad` for voice activity detection
- `kaudio` for resampling (24kHz → 16kHz)
- `rubato` for audio resampling (indirect dependency)

## Next Steps
- Fix long clip truncation (see trx issue for buffer trim safety limit)
- Add safety limit to prevent infinite empty-chunk loops
- Fix benchmark script IPv6 address
- Investigate server startup crash

title: SetEngine switch kills the WebSocket: old session finalize() closes the shared sink
SetEngine switch kills the WebSocket: old session finalize() closes the shared sink
description:
Reproduced live with the trailing-word probe (scripts/probe_trailing_word.py): on a server with 2+ engines, sending {"type":"setengine"} mid-connection kills the WebSocket.

Root cause: on SetEngine the server allocates the new session with the SAME shared SessionSink, then calls old.request_stop(). The old engine session finalizes and SessionState::finalize() (src/server/parallel.rs) ends with sink.close(), which sends Message::Close on the shared channel — the writer task closes the socket, and every subsequent message from the NEW session fails with 'failed to forward message to websocket writer'. The client sees close code 1005 mid-stream.

Also affects same-engine setengine? No — same-engine requests only re-send enginechanged. Only cross-engine switches are affected.

Fix direction: SessionSink needs per-session close ownership (e.g. close only when the sink is the session's own, or add EngineSession::release()/finalize_without_close for engine switches), or handle_connection should allocate a fresh sink per session and merge the channels.
